status.note: The most-used component in any library, and the first whose value is free text rather than a boolean or one of a fixed set. Sourced from the HTML input specification; the ARIA APG has no text-field pattern because the native element already is one.

intent.purpose: Collects a single line of text from a person. It is the control itself, where Field is the plumbing around a control — the two compose, and neither does the other's job.
behaviour: Holds a string, controlled via `value` + `onValueChange` or uncontrolled via `defaultValue`.
Reports every keystroke, not only the final answer, so a caller may validate as the person types or wait until they leave.
Shows placeholder text only while empty. Placeholder is never a label: it disappears exactly when the person needs it most, and it is the wrong contrast for reading.
Renders nothing about validity itself. Whether this text is acceptable is a Field's decision, and duplicating it here would let the two disagree.
notFor: More than one line. A growing box has different keyboard behaviour — Enter inserts a newline rather than submitting — and is a different contract.
Numbers with a range. That is a slider or a number input with min and max; a text field cannot express bounds.
Choosing from a set. That is a select or a combobox.
Passwords, without a way to reveal them. A masked field with no reveal control fails anyone who cannot type it twice from memory.

value.description: The text itself. Free-form: not a boolean, and not one of a fixed set — which is what makes this the first state in the library that `values` cannot describe.
value.visual: The text appears in the box. An empty field shows its placeholder instead.

disabled.description: The platform's own disabled state. Removed from the focus order and cannot be typed into.
disabled.visual: The box and its text dim, and the text cursor is dropped.

read-only.description: The text can be read and selected but not changed. Distinct from disabled, which removes it from the focus order.
read-only.visual: The box loses its editable affordance but keeps its text at full contrast.

invalid.description: Set from outside — usually by a surrounding Field. This component does not decide it.
invalid.visual: The box takes its error border.

hover.description: The pointer is over the box and it is not disabled.
hover.visual: The border takes its hover treatment.

focus-visible.visual: A ring is drawn around the box.

size.description: A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

a11y.keyboard: Every keyboard behaviour here belongs to the platform's text editing: selection, word movement, undo. This component adds none and must not intercept any.
notes: This component has NO accessible name of its own. It must be given one — by a surrounding Field, a `<label>`, or `aria-label`. A text field with only a placeholder is announced as unnamed, and the placeholder vanishes the moment someone types.

Placeholder text is not a label and must not be used as one. It disappears on the first keystroke, it fails contrast at most designs' placeholder colour, and it is not announced as a name by every screen reader.

`invalid` is set from outside and reaches the DOM as `aria-invalid`. Nothing here checks that a message explaining the failure exists — that is Field's job, and a field marked invalid with no message says only that something is wrong.

children.description: None. The value is text, not content.

root.description: The box. Owns the border, the ring and the text.
